name: Client data leaks to an AI service
event: Remote staff paste a client contact list into an AI tool; customer information is retained or exposed.
why: Frequent AI use and no prompt controls make exposure plausible; personal-data impact stays severe.
response: Approved enterprise tools, input minimization, restricted-data gate and retention review
proof: Verified data-flow review, DLP tests and supplier retention settings

name: Remote AI or ad account takeover
event: A stolen freelancer session grants access to campaign or AI workspaces.
affected: Clients, remote workers and the agency
why: Distributed identities and uneven MFA expand exposure; stolen sessions can still cause major harm.
response: SSO, phishing-resistant MFA, managed devices, least privilege and rapid revocation
proof: IdP/endpoint evidence and access revocation drill

name: Prompt injection triggers unsafe actions
event: Untrusted lead or web text instructs the assistant to disclose data or misuse connectors.
why: External text is routinely processed; isolated tools reduce opportunity, not the consequence of a bypass.
response: Treat external text as data, constrain connectors and gate external actions
proof: Adversarial end-to-end model/connector tests; not demonstrated by metadata simulation

name: Fabricated claims reach customers
event: AI invents a product guarantee or policy that is published or repeated by support.
why: Generative outputs can be inaccurate; reviewed source material and sign-off lower likelihood.
response: Approved source material, independent fact checks, human release and escalation
proof: Claim-verification sample and revision-bound publication approvals

name: Unfair or intrusive audience targeting
event: Lead labels infer sensitive characteristics and exclude or manipulate groups.
why: Proxy attributes can bias categories; harm remains material even after review.
response: Prohibit sensitive profiling; review consent, proxies and subgroup outcomes
proof: Use-case impact review with affected-user input and representative test data

name: Supplier reuses or transfers client inputs
event: An unreviewed supplier trains on prompts or stores client data in an unexpected region.
why: Supplier terms and subprocessors are unknown; contractual and technical checks reduce exposure.
response: Review processing roles, training opt-out, locations, deletion and exit terms
proof: Signed terms, settings export and documented transfer assessment where applicable

name: Unlicensed or misleading synthetic creative
event: Generated assets copy protected work or depict a person without permission.
affected: Rights holders, depicted people and consumers
why: Creative provenance is currently absent; documented review reduces avoidable release errors.
response: Rights/provenance checklist, likeness consent and contextual disclosure
proof: Asset rights log and documented synthetic-media release review

name: Deepfake instruction causes payment fraud
event: A synthetic executive voice persuades a remote employee to change a payee.
why: Remote requests can impersonate leaders; known-channel callback and dual approval reduce likelihood.
response: AI cannot pay; independently verify payee changes and require dual authorization
proof: Finance control walkthrough and callback tabletop

name: Shadow AI bypasses governance
event: Staff use personal tools outside the inventory to process client work.
why: Tool sprawl is assumed common; training and sanctioned access reduce but do not eliminate bypass.
response: Approved tools, easy request route, training and proportionate access monitoring
proof: Inventory reconciliation and access/training coverage report

name: AI outage or runaway workflow disrupts delivery
event: A provider failure or repeated tool loop delays support and consumes unexpected budget.
why: External service dependency is material; quotas and manual fallback limit frequency of disruption.
response: Usage caps, circuit breaker, human fallback and tested disable/retire process
proof: Quota/circuit-breaker logs, outage exercise and recovery verification
